title: Box Plot Anatomy
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Hover over or click the seven numbered parts of a box plot of 21 quiz scores to read what each part means, its value in the data, and the pandas code that computes it.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to identify the seven parts of a box plot and recall what each one represents.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Labeled diagram with hover and click to reveal, plus a hide-the-names self-test
keyQuestions: Which part of the box plot shows the middle 50% of the data?
Why does the lower whisker stop at 41 when the lower fence is at 28?
What would change in the plot if the score of 97 were 80 instead?
commonMisconceptions: The whiskers always reach the smallest and largest values (they stop at the most extreme values inside the fences, and anything beyond is drawn as an outlier).
The whisker ends sit exactly at Q1 − 1.5 × IQR and Q3 + 1.5 × IQR (the fences only decide which values count as outliers).
The line in the box is the mean (it is the median).
A longer half of the box holds more data (each half holds about a quarter of the values, and a longer half means those values are more spread out).
assessmentOpportunities: Given an unlabeled box plot, students label the median, Q1, Q3, both whisker ends, the IQR, and any outliers, and write the two fence formulas.
